Title: Nurses and Midwives: A force for change towards a better tomorrow
NewsSummary: The School of Nursing and Midwifery and Department of Nursing Services, Aga Khan University Hospital jointly celebrated the International Nurses Day and International Day of the Midwife on May 21, 2015.
NewsContent:
"The School of Nursing and Midwifery and Department of Nursing Services, Aga Khan University Hospital jointly celebrated the International Nurses Day and International Day of the Midwife on May 21, 2015. This year the theme for IND is 'Nurses: A Force for Change: Care Effective, Cost Effective' whereas for the IDM, it is 'Midwives: for Better Tomorrow'.

The programme aimed at acknowledging the services of the largest healthcare profession across the world and the fact that comprehensive financing for the health system may help achieve quality of care in a cost effective way.

Dr Yasmin Amarsi, Professor and Founding Dean, SONAM, East Africa stressed the importance of nursing and midwifery in today's healthcare landscape. "Nurses and midwives are an integral part of the healthcare force. Harmony of other disciplines with nursing and midwifery will make them better able to deliver quality care," said Dr Amarsi.

A panel discussion followed. During the discussion Hans Kederizki, Chief Executive Officer, Aga Khan University Hospital spoke about the role of nurses in achieving cost effective healthcare delivery. He was of the opinion that nurses are at the core of attaining high quality, access and cost balance in the healthcare sector and it is essential that nurses and policy makers focus on the role of nursing in providing quality care in a cost effective way.

Arusa Lakhani, Assistant Professor and Director Midwifery Programme, SONAM, AKU highlighted the significance of 

midwifery-led practice and its effects on care and cost effective healthcare delivery. She said that evidence shows that midwife led care is cost-effective, affordable and sustainable. "The challenge is to invest in higher education for midwives," she added.

Talking about the role of nurses and midwives working in the community, Dr Rashida Ahmed, Professor and Chairperson, Aga Khan Health Services, Pakistan shed light on how lady health visitors have transformed the health scenario in Northern areas of Pakistan and have made key developments towards achieving of Millennium Development Goals in a cost effective manner.

Prior to the event, five workshops were organised as part of the IND and IDM celebrations from May 18-19, 2015. They served the purpose of elaborating on the IND and IDM themes and covered topics such as planning care and cost effective research and tackling technology with cost. All workshops were well attended by nurses, undergraduate and graduate students, midwives, and other healthcare professionals from AKU and various nursing and medical institutions".
